quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and turn slightly into the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red traffic light means:

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to drive in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction shown by the arrow. Only proceed if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals help other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have large areas near the back that their mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and can focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, and makes headlight glare harder to recover from. It also reduces your inhibitions and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you to drive carefully because the road may be wet and slippery.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to re-enter the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to pull back onto the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if no other traffic is coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see if another vehicle is in that area.

questions.question: In fog, should you use your low beam headlights?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes.

questions.question: You come to a blocked intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot get all the way through. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: When should you slow down to exit a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first, then slow down. Do not start slowing down before entering the exit lane.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop. Release the gas pedal first to let your car slow. Then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: The best way to avoid losing control on wet roads is to drive faster.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride on water and cause hydroplaning. This makes you lose control. Slow down when driving in wet conditions to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Heat makes this worse by releasing more oil.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same as on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your distance from the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, must you yield to oncoming bicycles?
questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming bicycles like you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal means the same thing as:
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, no stopping, standing, or parking is allowed at any time.
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in someone's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It warns that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. Stay on the side shown by the arrow.

questions.question: To avoid headlight glare at night, you should look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, keep your eyes on the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles may cross or ride next to traffic here.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Defending yourself against poor drivers by passing them.
Following the vehicle ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that mirrors cannot show. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear. Then slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right lane if possible. If no right lane exists, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce speed. This lets the tailgater pass you. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Eating can slow alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from drinking too much.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light is a warning. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What is the correct way to back up?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow line to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction can cross the lines, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. Passing over a solid yellow line is not allowed.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisle next to a handicap parking space?
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These aisles provide space for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only to the left and right of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: You miss your exit on a freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, drive to the next exit or turn-around point. Do not back up. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: Are headlights legally required when people or vehicles cannot be seen from 1,000 feet away?
questions.explanation: Headlights must be used from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise. They must also be on whenever people or vehicles cannot be clearly seen from 1,000 feet away.

questions.question: When turning left, which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you can turn left in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean? When can you stop?

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagging person, or a train whistle. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A sign with a red circle and red slash means no. This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not permitted.

questions.question: How do you pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Move into the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must move into the oncoming traffic lane. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned to make a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cross lanes of traffic to make any turn.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.
